example.title: E-commerce Cart: Complete Spec Example
example.p: A fully-populated SDD spec for a Shopping Cart feature covering all required sections: problem statement, personas, user stories, FR/NFR, acceptance criteria, out-of-scope, dependencies, and preliminary data model.

section.title: Problem Statement
section.p: WHO: Online shoppers on an e-commerce platform. PROBLEM: Cannot save products for later purchase or manage multiple items before checkout. IMPACT: Users abandon purchases due to friction, reducing conversion rate from 2.1% baseline. SOLUTION: Persistent shopping cart with quantity management and price calculation. SUCCESS METRIC: Increase conversion rate from 2.1% to 3.5%.

section.title: User Personas
section.note: Persona 1: Busy Parent "Sarah" — Role: Working parent shopping for household items. Goal: Add items throughout the week and checkout once. Pain: Forgets items, no time for multiple checkout sessions. Context: Mobile during commute, desktop at home.

Persona 2: Deal Hunter "Mike" — Role: Budget-conscious shopper comparing prices. Goal: Save items, wait for sales, then purchase. Pain: Items disappear from browser, can't track prices. Context: Multiple devices, checks daily.

Two personas by design (r-two-personas-minimum): Sarah drives the "quick add" UX; Mike drives the "persistence across sessions" requirement. Different personas justify different acceptance criteria that would otherwise look redundant.

section.title: User Stories and Functional Requirements
section.p: US-001: As Sarah, I want to add products with one click so I can save items for later checkout. Priority: Must. Traces to: AC-001, AC-002. US-002: As a shopper, I want to change quantities so I can adjust my order. Priority: Must. Traces to: AC-003. US-003: As a shopper, I want to remove products. Priority: Must. Traces to: AC-004. US-004: As Mike, I want my cart to persist across sessions. Priority: Must. Traces to: AC-005, AC-006.

list.item: FR-001: System SHALL allow adding products to cart (US-001). Validation: product must be in stock; duplicate adds increase quantity; max 99 per product.
FR-002: System SHALL update cart total in real-time (US-001).
FR-003: System SHALL allow quantity updates 1-99 (US-002).
FR-004: System SHALL allow removing items (US-003).
FR-005: System SHALL persist cart for logged-in users (US-004).
FR-006: System SHALL use localStorage for guest users, expire after 7 days (US-004).

section.title: Non-Functional Requirements

list.item: NFR-001 Performance: Add-to-cart operation < 200ms p95 client-side. Validation: load test with 50k concurrent users. [SOURCE REQUIRED — replace with real measurement]
NFR-002 Scalability: Support 50k concurrent cart operations. [SOURCE REQUIRED]
NFR-003 Availability: Cart data recovery RTO < 1 min.
NFR-004 Usability: Cart visible in 1 click from any page.

section.note: Per r-nfr-source-required: the 200ms / 50k figures are plausible for a mid-scale platform but have no basis in any specific project.

section.title: Acceptance Criteria
section.note: AC-001 Happy Path: Given product "Wireless Mouse $25" in stock and empty cart. When user clicks "Add to Cart". Then: product added, badge shows "1", total shows "$25.00", success message 2s, product page stays.
AC-002 Duplicate: Given cart has "Wireless Mouse" qty 1. When user clicks "Add to Cart" again. Then: qty becomes 2, total "$50.00", no duplicate entry.
AC-003 Quantity Update: Given cart has "Wireless Mouse" qty 2. When user changes qty to 5. Then: total "$125.00", DB/localStorage updates within 500ms.
AC-004 Remove: Given cart has 2 products (total $75). When user removes "Wireless Mouse $25". Then: product gone, total "$50.00", badge updates.
AC-005 Logged-in Persistence: Given logged-in user with "Wireless Mouse" in cart. When browser closed and reopened 2 days later after login. Then: cart still contains item with current price.
AC-006 Guest Persistence: Given guest user with "Wireless Mouse". When browser closed and returned within 7 days. Then: cart still contains item.
section.p: Coverage matrix: [x] Happy path [x] Duplicate adds [x] Quantity limits [x] Persistence logged-in [x] Guest persistence [ ] Security (cart tampering) — documented risk [ ] Performance (large carts) — documented risk

section.title: Out of Scope

list.item: Save for Later — Phase 2
Share Cart via URL — Phase 3 (complexity)
Cart Price Alerts — Not planned (external dependency)
Multi-currency — v2.0 (international expansion only)

section.note: Per r-out-of-scope-when-column: the "Out of Scope / When" column is the highest-ROI section for preventing feature creep mid-sprint. Copy this pattern into every spec.

list.item: Constraint: Max 50 unique products per cart (DB performance)
Constraint: Max 99 quantity per product (business rule)
Constraint: localStorage max 5MB (browser limit)
Internal dep: Product Catalog (feature 01) — must be done
Internal dep: User Authentication (feature 02) — for logged-in cart
External dep: PostgreSQL database
External dep: Redis for cart session caching
Blocks: Checkout (feature 04)

section.title: Preliminary Data Model
section.note: Per r-data-model-preliminary: the spec model is intent only; the approved model lives in design.md after architectural decisions are made.

section.title: Open Questions

list.item: Should cart merge when guest user logs in? (cart merge on login is the most commonly overlooked question in cart specs)
How to handle out-of-stock items already in cart?
Show "X people have this in cart" social proof?

section.note: Per r-open-questions-required: open questions are forcing functions: unanswered, they become assumptions in design.md. Documented, they become explicit review targets before approval.

example.title: Using the Cart Example as a Few-Shot Reference
example.p: How to use this worked example when generating or reviewing specs, including key reusable patterns and AI-agent failure modes specific to this example. The failure modes live in content/03-failure-modes.xml.

list.item: FR → US traceability table: every FR row has a Traces To column pointing to US-X
NFR measurement format: requirement + target + measurement method + validation load test
AC Given/When/Then with specific values: "$25.00" not "valid price", "2 days later" not "some time"
Out of Scope with "When" column: Phase 2 / Phase 3 / v2.0 / Not planned
AC coverage matrix with explicit unchecked items as documented risks
Open Questions as a forcing function — minimum 3 per complex feature

section.title: Prompt Patterns
section.note: Few-shot generation prompt: "Use the following completed spec as a reference for structure and quality. Reference spec: [paste content/01-full-spec.xml]. Now write a spec for: [new feature name]. Problem: [problem statement]. User types: [list]. Key constraints: [list]. Follow the same section structure. Replace all domain-specific content. NFRs must use [MEASURE_NEEDED] where targets are unknown."
The prompt names content/01-full-spec.xml; that spec now lives in this file as the "E-commerce Cart: Complete Spec Example" group above — paste that group.

Gap analysis prompt: "Compare this draft spec against the e-commerce cart example. Identify: (1) sections present in example but missing from draft, (2) AC scenarios (error, edge case, persistence) missing from draft, (3) traceability gaps (FR with no AC, US with no FR). Output: gap list only."
